steps: Check the fireplace
Code-complying fireplace only, never a factory-built one. Minimum opening 29" W x 22" H x 19" D; confirm clearances and floor protection first.

Consult the authority having jurisdiction about the need for a permit before installation.

Min. opening29" (737 mm) W x 22" (559 mm) H x 19" (483 mm) D
Floor protection, front16" USA · 18" Canada
Floor protection, each side8"

Not to be installed in any factory-built fireplace (voids any and all warranties). Do not use a grate or elevate the fire. Do not obstruct combustion air openings or the space beneath the appliance.
Chimney liner + air supply
Continuous 6" liner from the appliance to the top of the chimney, insulated stainless recommended; 15 ft recommended minimum vertical height at sea level. Fresh-air inlet recommended in tight homes.

• Liner: 6" stainless steel listed to UL 1777, or the Class 3 requirements of CAN/ULC-S635, or CAN/ULC-S640.
  • Never connect to a chimney flue serving another appliance (voids the warranty).
  • Fasten all venting joints with sheet metal screws; run a bead of furnace cement around the flue collar connection.
  • Higher elevations and elbows raise the recommended height (table, p. 13).
  • Airtight homes: account for HRVs, air handlers, range hoods and dryers; a fresh air intake into the room is recommended to avoid air starvation, smoke spillage and carbon monoxide.
Masonry chimney prep
Have it inspected and cleaned: no cracks, loose mortar, deterioration or blockage; inner cross-section recommended no less than the flue area (28in²). Tag the fireplace if it was altered.

• Inspection by a certified professional to National Fire Protection Association minimum standards.
  • Chimney at least three feet above the highest point where it passes through the roof and two feet higher than any part of the building within ten feet.
  • If the fireplace is modified, fasten the manufacturer-supplied metal tag with screws or nails where it will be seen if the insert is removed: "This fireplace has been altered to accommodate a fireplace insert and should be inspected by a qualified person prior to re-use as a conventional fireplace."
Note: the certification label says do not remove bricks or mortar in the masonry fireplace (p. 4); p. 12 says masonry or steel, including the damper plate, may be removed from the smoke shelf and adjacent damper frame to fit a liner, provided this doesn't weaken the structure or reduce protection for combustibles.
Remove the flue collar
From inside the firebox, remove the two nuts with a 9/16" wrench and take the flue collar assembly out the rear. Check its gasket is intact and adhered.
Thermostat rod

Check the fans haven't shifted in transit. With the thermostat fully open (set screw on the stop), slide the rod in from the left, interlock the machined faces and tighten the set-collar grub screw. Knob pointer straight down when fully open.
Lower shroud + wiring

Mount the power cord on the side nearest the outlet and plug the unused slot; fit the rheostat and knob; slide the ash shelf onto the brackets (5/32" allen key); connect wires by label and fit the ground screw.

• Lift the lower shroud to clear the thermostat cover while fitting it.
  • Cord out the right side: zip-tie any excess wire clear of the fan.
  • Rheostat pins must protrude through the alignment holes.
  • Three-prong grounded plug into a grounded three-hole receptacle; never cut the grounding prong or route the cord in front of or under the appliance.

The lower shroud front cover is fitted during the upper shroud step.
Level the insert

Through the lower shroud opening, adjust the four corner levelling bolts. Fill any space underneath only with non-combustible material (firebrick); the two supplied metal strips help it slide over a rough hearth.
Upper shroud

Lay the thermometer wire across the ash shelf, lock the rear shroud onto the screws, fasten the catalytic thermometer (two screws), fit the lower shroud cover, then hang the front upper shroud (magnets hold its bottom).
Liner to flue collar

Attach the liner to the flue collar assembly so it hangs roughly 2' (607 mm) above the fireplace floor. Through the open loading and bypass doors, pull it onto the bolts, tighten evenly, close the bypass and slide the insert home.

1. Attach the dropped liner securely to the flue collar assembly; it should hang roughly 2' (607 mm) above the fireplace floor.
  2. Open the loading door.
  3. Open the bypass door so you can reach up through the appliance to the hanging collar.
  4. Pull it down to line the bolts up with the holes in the rear of the firebox, then pull forward so it slides along the top of the firebox and the gasket seats. Feel the joint: a gap means it isn't seated, so realign.
  5. Fasten with the original hardware, tightening the nuts evenly.
  6. Close the bypass door before sliding the insert into its final position.

To remove the insert for inspection, do steps 1 to 4 in reverse.
Record the install
Fill in the installer notes on the back page (dealer, installer, phone, date installed, serial no.) and leave the manual with the homeowner.

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Build every fire right on the firebricks, with all the bricks in place. Don't use a grate.

  1. Turn the thermostat to HIGH and the fan (if you have one) off.
  2. Open the bypass door, then the loading door.
  3. Put 10 balls of non-glossy paper toward the front of the firebox. Crisscross 20 pieces of kindling on top, with air gaps.
  4. Light it and leave the loading door cracked open. Don't leave it unattended.
  5. When the kindling is fully burning, add two or three medium logs. Keep the door unlatched until they catch.
  6. Latch the door. When the catalyst temperature starts to climb, close the bypass door. Leaving the door open after the wood catches can make the combustor fail early.
  7. When nearly all the wood is burning and the gauge is in the active zone, open the bypass and loading doors and finish loading, as far back as you can. Latch the door and close the bypass.
  8. Leave it on HIGH until the fire is well established, then turn the thermostat down gradually.
Note: the manual gives three different times to turn the fan on: to high once the bypass is closed (step 7, p. 23), after the initial warm up (step 11, p. 23), and not until the stove reaches normal operating temperature (p. 18).
First fires: the paint cures and gives off a strong odor and some smoke. Burn at a low setting for several hours and open a door or window. A change in paint color is normal.

heat.title: Setting the heat
heat.html:
The thermostat knob is on the lower left side of the front. At HIGH the insert burns fastest and gives the most heat. Turn it counterclockwise for a slower burn and less heat.

  • Change the setting gradually. Turning it too fast can make the thermostat work poorly.
  • Your house, chimney and weather all affect the burn rate, so expect to try a few positions.
  • Don't be afraid to fill the firebox. The wood only burns as fast as the thermostat allows.
  • On a low setting you may see very little flame. If the gauge stays in the active zone, the burn is continuing.
  • Turning it down can make the catalyst temperature climb for up to several hours. That's normal.

How low can it go?

The manual shows the tested low-burn knob position as a picture on p. 25. Turn it too low and the fire may go out or the catalyst stop working (needle in the inactive zone). If that happens, turn it back up and let the fire re-establish.

Fans (if fitted)

About 30 minutes after the fire is established, match the fan speed to the thermostat: low with low, medium with medium, high with high.

The thermostat is set at the factory. Don't tamper with it.

reload.title: Reloading
reload.html:
Check the gauge first. If the needle is still in the active (red) zone, follow these steps. If it has dropped into the inactive (white) zone, use the lighting steps instead.

  1. Have the next load ready. Turn the thermostat to HIGH and wait 2 minutes.
  2. To cut down on smoke, you can open the bypass door and wait another 2 minutes.
  3. Crack the loading door open to let room air in. Give it about a minute.
  4. Open the door slowly and load. If a lot of smoke spills out, close the door slightly until the chimney draws again.
  5. Latch the door and close the bypass right away (if you opened it). Leave it on HIGH for 20 to 30 minutes, or until the fire is very well established, then turn it down.
When to reload: the gauge only shows the catalyst temperature. Use it as a hint, along with how much wood is left and whether the room is cooling.

Load wood only in the usable loading area the manual shades in its diagram on p. 22. Loading beyond it voids the warranty and is a safety hazard.

bypass.title: Bypass door & catalyst gauge
bypass.html:
The bypass door

Inside the top of the firebox, the bypass door lets smoke skip the catalytic combustor for a while. You open it when lighting, and can open it when reloading. Closed, the exhaust goes through the combustor.

  • To open: hook the bypass handle on the side of the bypass latch and pull the rod out.
  • To close: put the handle on the center of the latch and push in.
Never touch the bypass latch itself. It can cause serious burns. Always use the bypass handle (it comes in the manual kit).

The catalyst gauge

The catalytic thermometer only tells you whether the combustor is working. Red is the active zone. White is inactive: the combustor is below 500F and may not be burning clean. In normal use the needle stays in one spot in the red.

A bypass door left open gives too much heat and more creosote in the chimney, so close it once the fire is going.

wood.title: What wood to burn
wood.html:
Burn natural cord wood only. To get it to 20% moisture or lower, split it, stack it so air reaches all of it, and keep it out of rain and snow for at least 24 months. Hardwood and softwood both burn well; dense hardwood burns a little slower and longer.

Check it with a moisture meter

  1. Pick three logs at random and split each down the middle.
  2. On each split face, take three readings: 2" from each end and one in the middle, pins in line with the grain.
  3. Average all the readings. It's an approximate figure.

Never burn

  • Wet, green or unseasoned wood. It can build up too much creosote. If that ignites, it can cause a chimney fire that may become a house fire and cause serious bodily harm.
  • Salt-water driftwood. It corrodes the insert and voids the warranty.
  • Treated wood, coal, charcoal, colored paper, cardboard, solvents or garbage. Burning these may release toxic fumes and/or carbon monoxide, which may result in poisoning.
  • Flammable fluids such as gasoline, naphtha or engine gel.
  • Never use chemicals or fluids such as gasoline-type lantern fuel, kerosene or charcoal lighter fluid to start or freshen up a fire. Doing so may lead to over-firing, resulting in a house fire and serious bodily harm.
Lots of small, very dry pieces, offcuts or pressed logs can overheat the firebox and damage it and the catalyst. Don't use them as your main fuel.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
The best way to keep the glass clean is to burn on high for a while after every reload. New wood gives off moisture that carries creosote onto the glass, and burning it off early helps. Before an overnight low burn, leave the thermostat higher for 30 minutes to an hour first.

Long stretches on a very low setting leave dark deposits. Run it on HIGH for about 30 minutes to burn most of them off.

Cleaning by hand

  • Only when the insert and the glass are cool.
  • Use a soft cloth and no abrasive cleaners.
  • After any cleaner, rinse the glass well with water. Leftover cleaner bakes on and is very hard to remove.
Don't strike the glass or slam the door, and don't use the insert if the glass or its gasket is broken. Replace the glass only with 5mm ceramic glass. The warranty covers glass for thermal breakage only.

care.title: Ashes & routine care
care.html:
Do all of this with the fire out and the insert cool. The glass and surfaces stay hot for a long time.

Ashes

  • Take ashes out when they come within one inch of the door opening, but leave a bed about 1/2" thick. Wood burns best on it.
  • Use a metal container with a tight-fitting lid, with nothing else in it. Set it on a noncombustible floor or outside on the ground, well away from anything that burns. Keep it closed until the cinders are fully cool.
Never store hot ashes in a garage or basement. They give off carbon monoxide and flammable gases.

During the season

  • Look at the catalytic combustor at least three times a season. If its face has deposits, lift off the flame shield and brush the face gently with a soft paint brush. Never scrape it.
  • Check the door seal with a paper test: shut the door on a dollar bill and pull it out. No resistance means the door needs adjusting.
  • Check that the thermostat works, and that the fans run and are free of dust, lint and ash.
  • After the last fire of the season, remove all the ash, then clean out and inspect the insert. Problems you find must be corrected before the next season, or the warranty is void.

Thermostat or thermometer repairs are for a certified installer. Ask your dealer.

chimney.title: Chimney, creosote & chimney fires
chimney.html:
Slow fires make tar and vapors that condense in the cooler chimney as creosote. If it ignites, it burns extremely hot. Hotter fires leave less behind.

  • Inspect the chimney regularly in the heating season, especially the coldest months, until you know how often it needs cleaning.
  • Have the chimney and the insert cleaned at least once a year, or as often as needed. A professional chimney sweep is recommended.
  • Open the bypass door before sweeping so soot falls into the firebox.

If a chimney fire starts

  1. Turn the thermostat knob fully counterclockwise. Make sure the loading door and bypass door are tightly closed.
  2. Call the fire department.
  3. Check the chimney, attic and roof for anything hot enough to catch fire. If needed, use a fire extinguisher or a garden hose.
  4. Don't use the insert again until a certified chimney sweep has inspected the chimney and you're sure it isn't damaged.
Chimney-fire damage isn't covered by the warranty. Make sure everyone at home knows the plan.
Very cold weather: water vapor can freeze in the chimney and block it. Burn on HIGH for 5 to 10 minutes to melt any ice.

safety.title: Safety around the insert
safety.html:
• The insert is hot while it's running. Keep children and pets from touching it.
  • Keep furniture, clothing and anything else that can burn at least 48" from the front. Don't store firewood within the clearances or the space you need for loading and ash removal.
  • Run it with the loading door closed. Open it only to add wood, and don't leave the insert unattended while you light it.
  • Don't block the air openings or the space beneath the insert.
  • Never run it without the catalytic combustor or flame shield, or with the door gasket or glass missing or damaged.
  • Have at least one smoke detector and one carbon monoxide monitor in the same room, and a fire extinguisher everyone knows about. If an alarm sounds, get everyone out.

Signs of over-firing

If the insert or the chimney glows, it's over-firing. Later you may see warped plates and burnt-off paint. Things that lead to it: small or wrong fuel, leaving the door open too long, and worn gaskets. Over-firing can seriously damage the insert and voids the warranty.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Blaze King's limited warranty covers the original purchaser of an insert bought from an authorized dealer and installed in the USA or Canada. It starts on the date of purchase and can't be transferred.

Catalytic combustor6 years
Stove body, steel firebox components5 years
Fan assemblies, modular thermostat, door handle steel parts2 years
All parts and materials, incl. paint finish1 year

You share the cost later on. Combustor: no charge for the first three years, then you pay 60%, 70% and 80% of the then-current retail price in years 4, 5 and 6. For parts warranted beyond the first year under the five-year coverage, you pay 20% of the then-current retail cost in year 2, 40% in year 3, 60% in year 4 and 80% in year 5.

Not covered, or voids it

  • Gaskets and firebrick; glass except thermal breakage.
  • Over-firing, salt-water driftwood, treated wood, chimney-fire damage.
  • Installing it in a factory-built fireplace or on a chimney serving another appliance.
Report a problem to your dealer within 30 days of finding it, with proof of purchase. This is a summary; the full terms are in the manual.

conflicts.issue: Certification label electrical rating: 0.58 Amps in the English text vs 0,35 A in the French text (both 115 V, 60 Hz).
Thermal floor protection: label says UL 1682 type 2 (R=1.06) plus a 1/2" layer from flush to 5" below the firebox bottom; p. 10 says UL1618 Type 2, R=1.06 minimum, no thickness.
Catalytic combustor part number: label gives Combustor OEM #115-0335; p. 29 and the parts list (p. 41) give S.CAT2425.
conflicts.reason: Two numbering systems, not a misprint: the label's Combustor OEM #115-0335 is the combustor's OEM number; S.CAT2425 is Blaze King's own part number for the combustor assembly (p. 29, parts list p. 41). Both are shown.

conflicts.issue: Label says do not remove bricks or mortar in masonry fireplace; p. 12 allows removing masonry or steel, including the damper plate, from the smoke shelf and adjacent damper frame to fit a liner.

When to turn fans on at start-up: Lighting step 7 says on to high once the door is latched and the bypass closed; step 11 says after the initial warm up; Fan operation (p. 18) says off until normal operating temperature, then match the thermostat about 30 minutes after the fire is established.

review.notes: Shown only as figures or check-mark grids, so pointed to rather than transcribed: appliance dimensions for each shroud (pp. 7-9), wiring diagram (p. 14), usable loading area (p. 22), tested low-burn knob position (p. 25), warranty parts/labor grid (p. 43). Warranty periods come from the prose on p. 44 and item 24 on p. 46. The shoulder-season outdoor temperature range on p. 25 is garbled in the text extraction and was left out. The troubleshooting chart (p. 39) calls the catalytic thermometer 'on top of stove' while p. 20 places it in the lower left-hand corner of the surround; the guide gives no location. Install steps (pp. 14-15) assume fitted fans and a supplied rheostat, while pp. 18 and 32 call fans optional; owner text says 'if fitted'. Hearth-extension metric values differ by 1 mm between the label and p. 10; inch values agree, p. 10 metric used. The manual prints no efficiency figure (only the B415.1-10 HHV method), no burn time and no heating area, so the catalog's efficiency_pct, burn_time_hr_max and heating area can't be checked; the manual's 325 lb is a shipping weight; the catalog view_area isn't stated in the manual. Combustor replacement steps on p. 28 skip number 4. ft3 / m3 written as ft³ / m³.
